name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Huge GOP fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 5%
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but not partisan lean
model.rationale: The seat sits in territory about thirteen points Republican, the GOP nominee has outraised the Democrat by roughly 100-to-1 with substantial outside support, and markets give Democrats only about a 5% chance. With no polls or expert ratings to the contrary, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or a divisive Republican runoff could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Houston-area seat is strongly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about thirteen points toward the GOP. Morgan Luttrell's retirement puts a new Republican on the ballot, but the party's structural advantage remains intact.

Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann has raised over $2 million and drawn nearly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised about $22,000 with no outside spending. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 5% chance, and no polls or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive. The forecast points to a comfortable Republican hold, with modest uncertainty because it is an open seat with no polling.
